title: Support email triage
tagline: Sorts incoming customer emails by topic and urgency, then drafts a reply for a person to check.
what_it_does: A small online shop gets a few hundred customer emails a week. This script reads each one, decides what it is about (a refund, a late parcel, a broken item or something else) and how urgent it is.
It then looks up the order and drafts a reply in the shop's tone. A support agent reads every draft before it is sent.
built_with: Python, the Anthropic API, a CSV order table
diagram_caption: Blue steps are automated. The dashed orange step is done by a person.

input.Subject: Where is my kettle?
input.Body: Hi, I ordered a kettle (order EX-1001) nine days ago and the tracking has not moved since Monday. Could you check? Thanks, Jo

cases.label: Refund request, frustrated customer

input.Subject: REFUND NOW
input.Body: Third email. The lid snapped on day two. I want my money back, not another kettle.

cases.prompt_summary: Classify the email into one of four topics and an urgency from 1 to 3, then draft a reply that follows the shop's refund policy and tone rules.
cases.output_illustrative:
Topic: refund. Urgency: 3.

Hi Sam,

I'm sorry the lid broke so soon, and that you've had to write three times. I've started a full refund to your original payment method; you'll see it within 5 working days. You don't need to send the kettle back.

Best wishes,
The support team
